::: {.callout-note icon="true"}
## Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:

- validate the final analytical row count;
- confirm the uniqueness of `survey_cycle + SEQN`;
- verify survey-cycle coverage;
- assess Demographic match completeness;
- validate CBC and Demographic provenance;
- confirm required analytical variables;
- inspect missingness by cycle;
- identify impossible or implausible values;
- create a consolidated validation report;
- stop the pipeline when critical checks fail.
:::

## Why post-merge validation is necessary

A successful join does not prove that the resulting dataset is analytically valid.

The merged dataset could still contain:

- duplicated participant keys;
- missing survey cycles;
- unexpected row multiplication;
- missing required variables;
- incomplete Demographic matches;
- lost provenance;
- supplementary records;
- implausible laboratory values;
- structural missingness;
- inconsistent coding across cycles.

Post-merge validation converts these expectations into explicit checks.

## Where you are in the workflow

You currently have:

```r
cbc_demographics_1999_2018
```

This dataset was created using a one-to-one left join between:

```r
cbc_primary_1999_2018
```

and:

```r
demographics_1999_2018
```

The explicit merge key is:

```text
survey_cycle + SEQN
```

## Add the validation section

Add this below the merge section in `nhanes_pipeline.R`:

```r
# ============================================================
# SECTION 11: VALIDATE THE MERGED ANALYTICAL DATASET
# ============================================================
```

## Confirm the merged object exists

Run:

```r
if (
  !exists(
    "cbc_demographics_1999_2018"
  )
) {
  stop(
    "The merged analytical dataset does not exist."
  )
}
```

Confirm that it is a data frame:

```r
if (
  !is.data.frame(
    cbc_demographics_1999_2018
  )
) {
  stop(
    "The merged analytical object is not a data frame."
  )
}
```

## Record the final dimensions

Run:

```r
final_dataset_dimensions <- tibble::tibble(
  rows = nrow(
    cbc_demographics_1999_2018
  ),
  columns = ncol(
    cbc_demographics_1999_2018
  )
)
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  final_dataset_dimensions
)
```

## Validate row-count preservation

The merged dataset should contain exactly the same number of rows as the primary CBC dataset.

Run:

```r
final_row_count_validation <- tibble::tibble(
  primary_cbc_rows =
    nrow(
      cbc_primary_1999_2018
    ),
  merged_rows =
    nrow(
      cbc_demographics_1999_2018
    ),
  rows_preserved =
    primary_cbc_rows ==
      merged_rows
)
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  final_row_count_validation
)
```

Stop if the row count changed:

```r
if (
  !final_row_count_validation$rows_preserved
) {
  stop(
    "The final merged row count differs from the primary CBC row count."
  )
}
```

## Validate survey-cycle coverage

Define the expected cycles:

```r
expected_survey_cycles <- c(
  "1999-2000",
  "2001-2002",
  "2003-2004",
  "2005-2006",
  "2007-2008",
  "2009-2010",
  "2011-2012",
  "2013-2014",
  "2015-2016",
  "2017-2018"
)
```

Identify observed cycles:

```r
observed_survey_cycles <-
  sort(
    unique(
      cbc_demographics_1999_2018$survey_cycle
    )
  )
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  observed_survey_cycles
)
```

Find missing cycles:

```r
missing_survey_cycles <- setdiff(
  expected_survey_cycles,
  observed_survey_cycles
)
```

Find unexpected cycles:

```r
unexpected_survey_cycles <- setdiff(
  observed_survey_cycles,
  expected_survey_cycles
)
```

Stop if expected cycles are missing:

```r
if (
  length(
    missing_survey_cycles
  ) > 0
) {
  stop(
    "The final dataset is missing survey cycles: ",
    paste(
      missing_survey_cycles,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}
```

Stop if unexpected cycles appear:

```r
if (
  length(
    unexpected_survey_cycles
  ) > 0
) {
  stop(
    "The final dataset contains unexpected survey cycles: ",
    paste(
      unexpected_survey_cycles,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}
```

## Create a cycle-level row summary

Run:

```r
final_cycle_summary <-
  cbc_demographics_1999_2018 |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    survey_cycle
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    records =
      dplyr::n(),
    unique_participants =
      dplyr::n_distinct(
        SEQN
      ),
    duplicate_keys =
      records -
      unique_participants,
    matched_demographics =
      sum(
        demographic_match
      ),
    unmatched_demographics =
      sum(
        !demographic_match
      ),
    demographic_match_percent =
      100 *
      matched_demographics /
      records,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    match(
      survey_cycle,
      expected_survey_cycles
    )
  )
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  final_cycle_summary,
  n = Inf
)
```

## Validate CBC provenance

Define required CBC provenance columns:

```r
required_cbc_provenance <- c(
  "cbc_source_dataset_id",
  "cbc_source_component",
  "cbc_source_file_id",
  "cbc_source_exam",
  "cbc_analysis_role",
  "cbc_source_url",
  "cbc_local_source_file",
  "cbc_source_sha256"
)
```

Identify missing columns:

```r
missing_cbc_provenance <- setdiff(
  required_cbc_provenance,
  names(
    cbc_demographics_1999_2018
  )
)
```

Stop if any are missing:

```r
if (
  length(
    missing_cbc_provenance
  ) > 0
) {
  stop(
    "Missing CBC provenance columns: ",
    paste(
      missing_cbc_provenance,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}
```

Check missing CBC provenance values:

```r
cbc_provenance_missingness <-
  cbc_demographics_1999_2018 |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::all_of(
        required_cbc_provenance
      ),
      ~ sum(
        is.na(
          .x
        )
      )
    )
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = dplyr::everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "missing_values"
  )
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  cbc_provenance_missingness,
  n = Inf
)
```

Every CBC provenance field should be available for every primary CBC row.

## Validate required analytical variables

Define a small set of variables required for the tutorial analysis:

```r
required_analysis_variables <- c(
  "survey_cycle",
  "SEQN",
  "LBXHGB",
  "RIAGENDR"
)
```

Check:

```r
missing_analysis_variables <- setdiff(
  required_analysis_variables,
  names(
    cbc_demographics_1999_2018
  )
)
```

Stop if any are missing:

```r
if (
  length(
    missing_analysis_variables
  ) > 0
) {
  stop(
    "The final dataset is missing required analytical variables: ",
    paste(
      missing_analysis_variables,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}
```

::: {.callout-important icon="true"}
## Required variables should be analysis-specific

A pipeline can contain hundreds of variables.

Validation should identify the variables required for the declared analysis rather than assuming that every possible NHANES variable must be present.
:::

## Inspect key variable classes

Run:

```r
analysis_variable_classes <- tibble::tibble(
  variable = required_analysis_variables,
  variable_class = purrr::map_chr(
    required_analysis_variables,
    function(variable_name) {
      paste(
        class(
          cbc_demographics_1999_2018[[
            variable_name
          ]]
        ),
        collapse = "; "
      )
    }
  )
)
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  analysis_variable_classes
)
```

Confirm that:

- `survey_cycle` is character;
- `SEQN` is numeric;
- `LBXHGB` is numeric;
- `RIAGENDR` is numeric or labelled numeric.

## Inspect missingness in required variables

Run:

```r
required_variable_missingness <-
  cbc_demographics_1999_2018 |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::all_of(
        required_analysis_variables
      ),
      ~ sum(
        is.na(
          .x
        )
      )
    )
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = dplyr::everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "missing_values"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    total_records =
      nrow(
        cbc_demographics_1999_2018
      ),
    missing_percent =
      100 *
      missing_values /
      total_records
  )
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  required_variable_missingness,
  n = Inf
)
```

Missing laboratory or Demographic values do not necessarily indicate pipeline failure.

They must be interpreted using:

- component eligibility;
- specimen availability;
- examination status;
- cycle-specific structure;
- source documentation.

## Inspect hemoglobin distribution

Run:

```r
summary(
  cbc_demographics_1999_2018$LBXHGB
)
```

Create a cycle-level range report:

```r
hemoglobin_range_by_cycle <-
  cbc_demographics_1999_2018 |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    survey_cycle
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    nonmissing_records =
      sum(
        !is.na(
          LBXHGB
        )
      ),
    minimum =
      ifelse(
        all(
          is.na(
            LBXHGB
          )
        ),
        NA_real_,
        min(
          LBXHGB,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
      ),
    median =
      ifelse(
        all(
          is.na(
            LBXHGB
          )
        ),
        NA_real_,
        median(
          LBXHGB,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
      ),
    maximum =
      ifelse(
        all(
          is.na(
            LBXHGB
          )
        ),
        NA_real_,
        max(
          LBXHGB,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    match(
      survey_cycle,
      expected_survey_cycles
    )
  )
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  hemoglobin_range_by_cycle,
  n = Inf
)
```

## Flag clearly impossible hemoglobin values

For a basic data-integrity check, flag nonpositive values:

```r
nonpositive_hemoglobin <-
  cbc_demographics_1999_2018 |>
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(
      LBXHGB
    ),
    LBXHGB <= 0
  )
```

Count:

```r
nrow(
  nonpositive_hemoglobin
)
```

Values outside an expected clinical range may require review, but thresholds should not be used casually to delete observations.

::: {.callout-warning icon="true"}
## Plausibility flags are not automatic exclusion rules

An unusual value can reflect:

- a true extreme observation;
- a measurement issue;
- a coding issue;
- a unit difference;
- a changed method;
- a data-entry or release problem.

Flag first. Investigate before excluding.
:::

## Create a broad hemoglobin review flag

Use a deliberately broad review range:

```r
hemoglobin_review_flags <-
  cbc_demographics_1999_2018 |>
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(
      LBXHGB
    ),
    LBXHGB < 3 |
      LBXHGB > 25
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    survey_cycle,
    SEQN,
    LBXHGB,
    cbc_source_dataset_id,
    cbc_source_file_id
  )
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  hemoglobin_review_flags,
  n = Inf
)
```

This is a review list, not a deletion list.

## Identify available weight variables

Search the final dataset:

```r
available_weight_variables <- grep(
  "^WT",
  names(
    cbc_demographics_1999_2018
  ),
  value = TRUE
)
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  available_weight_variables
)
```

This step inventories available weights.

It does not determine which weight should be used for a specific analysis.

Weight selection depends on:

- the analytical component;
- examination eligibility;
- subsample design;
- number of combined cycles;
- NHANES weighting guidance.

## Create a consolidated validation table

Build one check table:

```r
final_validation_checks <- tibble::tibble(
  check = c(
    "merged_object_exists",
    "merged_is_data_frame",
    "primary_cbc_rows_preserved",
    "required_key_columns_present",
    "missing_composite_key_rows",
    "duplicate_composite_keys",
    "expected_survey_cycles_present",
    "unexpected_survey_cycles_absent",
    "demographic_match_present",
    "demographic_match_has_no_missing_values",
    "cbc_provenance_columns_present",
    "cbc_provenance_complete",
    "cbc_role_is_primary",
    "second_exam_absent",
    "one_primary_cbc_source_per_cycle",
    "required_analysis_variables_present",
    "sex_codes_valid",
    "survey_design_variables_present",
    "cbc_hashes_valid",
    "matched_demographic_hashes_valid"
  ),
  passed = c(
    exists(
      "cbc_demographics_1999_2018"
    ),
    is.data.frame(
      cbc_demographics_1999_2018
    ),
    final_row_count_validation$rows_preserved,
    length(
      missing_required_key_columns
    ) == 0,
    nrow(
      final_missing_key_rows
    ) == 0,
    nrow(
      final_duplicate_keys
    ) == 0,
    length(
      missing_survey_cycles
    ) == 0,
    length(
      unexpected_survey_cycles
    ) == 0,
    "demographic_match" %in%
      names(
        cbc_demographics_1999_2018
      ),
    sum(
      is.na(
        cbc_demographics_1999_2018$demographic_match
      )
    ) == 0,
    length(
      missing_cbc_provenance
    ) == 0,
    all(
      cbc_provenance_missingness$missing_values == 0
    ),
    all(
      cbc_demographics_1999_2018$cbc_analysis_role ==
        "primary"
    ),
    !"L25_2_B" %in%
      unique(
        cbc_demographics_1999_2018$cbc_source_file_id
      ),
    all(
      final_cbc_source_by_cycle$primary_cbc_sources == 1
    ),
    length(
      missing_analysis_variables
    ) == 0,
    nrow(
      unexpected_sex_codes
    ) == 0,
    length(
      missing_survey_design_variables
    ) == 0,
    nrow(
      invalid_cbc_hashes
    ) == 0,
    nrow(
      invalid_demographic_hashes
    ) == 0
  )
)
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  final_validation_checks,
  n = Inf
)
```

Stop when failures exist:

```r
if (
  nrow(
    failed_final_checks
  ) > 0
) {
  stop(
    "Final validation failed: ",
    paste(
      failed_final_checks$check,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}
```

## Validation does not replace scientific review

The checks in this lesson establish that the pipeline behaved as intended.

They do not prove that:

- every variable is harmonized correctly;
- laboratory methods are equivalent across cycles;
- the correct survey weight has been selected;
- all outliers are valid;
- a planned statistical model is appropriate;
- an unweighted summary is nationally representative.

Those questions require component documentation and analysis-specific review.

## Common mistakes

### Assuming a successful join is sufficient

A join can succeed while producing duplicate or incomplete records.

### Treating all missing values as errors

Some missingness reflects eligibility, specimen collection, component availability, or cycle structure.

### Deleting unusual laboratory values automatically

Unusual values should be flagged and investigated first.

### Using one weight for every analysis

Weight selection depends on the component, subsample, cycles, and analytical population.

### Validating only the final row count

Row counts are important, but keys, cycles, variables, provenance, match status, and value structure must also be checked.

### Ignoring failed checks

A validation table is useful only when the pipeline stops or clearly warns when critical expectations are violated.

## Checkpoint

Confirm:

- [ ] The merged object exists.
- [ ] The merged object is a data frame.
- [ ] The primary CBC row count was preserved.
- [ ] Required key columns are present.
- [ ] Composite-key values are complete.
- [ ] `survey_cycle + SEQN` is unique.
- [ ] All ten expected survey cycles are present.
- [ ] No unexpected cycles appear.
- [ ] `demographic_match` is logical and complete.
- [ ] Match status agrees with Demographic provenance.
- [ ] CBC provenance is complete.
- [ ] Only primary CBC records are present.
- [ ] `L25_2_B` is absent.
- [ ] Each cycle has one primary CBC source.
- [ ] Required analysis variables are present.
- [ ] `RIAGENDR` codes are valid.
- [ ] Hemoglobin missingness was summarized.
- [ ] Hemoglobin ranges were inspected.
- [ ] Review flags were saved without automatic deletion.
- [ ] Survey-design variables are present.
- [ ] Available weight variables were inventoried.
- [ ] Source hashes are valid.
- [ ] Critical validation checks passed.
- [ ] The validated RDS file was saved.

## Knowledge check

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Why should the final merged row count equal the primary CBC row count?

The merge uses the primary CBC dataset as the left analytical base. A one-to-one left join should add Demographic columns without adding or removing CBC rows.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Does an unusual hemoglobin value automatically mean the record should be deleted?

No. It should be flagged and investigated for measurement, coding, unit, method, or source issues before any exclusion decision is made.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Does passing pipeline validation make an unweighted analysis nationally representative?

No. National inference still requires the appropriate NHANES survey weights, strata, primary sampling units, and multi-cycle weighting procedures.
:::
